ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in the figure, draw $AD\perp BC$ at $D$, intersecting $EH$ at $M$, \\
$\because$ The area of $\triangle ABC$ is $36$, $BC=12$, \\
$\therefore$ $\frac{1}{2}BC\times AD=36$, \\
$\therefore$ $\frac{1}{2}\times 12\times AD=36$, \\
$\therefore$ $AD=6$, \\
$\because$ Square $EFGH$ is inscribed in $\angle ABC$, \\
$\therefore$ $EH\parallel FG$, let $EH=EF=FG=HG=x$, \\
$\therefore$ $\angle AEH=\angle B$, $\angle AHE=\angle C$, \\
$\therefore$ $\triangle AEH\sim \triangle ABC$, \\
$\therefore$ $\frac{AE}{AB}=\frac{EH}{BC}$, \\
$\because$ $AD\perp BC$, \\
$\therefore$ $\angle ADG=90^\circ$, \\
$\because$ $EH\parallel FG$, \\
$\therefore$ $\angle ADG=\angle AMH=90^\circ$, \\
$\therefore$ $AM\perp EH$, \\
Again, $\because$ $EH\parallel FG$, $AD\perp BC$, \\
$\therefore$ $DM=EF=EH=x$, $\frac{AE}{AB}=\frac{AM}{AD}$, \\
$\therefore$ $AM=6-x$, \\

raw_record.original_question: As shown in the figure, square $EFGH$ is inscribed in right-angled triangle $ABC$, with $\angle A=90^\circ$ and $BC=12$. If the area of $\triangle ABC$ is 36, what is the length of $EH$?
raw_record.answer: Solution: Draw $AD\perp BC$ at $D$, intersecting $EH$ at $M$. Since the area of $\triangle ABC$ is $36$ and $BC=12$, $\frac{1}{2}BC\times AD=36$, so $\frac{1}{2}\times 12\times AD=36$, hence $AD=6$. Since square $EFGH$ is inscribed in $\angle ABC$, $EH\parallel FG$. Let $EH=EF=FG=HG=x$. Then $\angle AEH=\angle B$ and $\angle AHE=\angle C$, so $\triangle AEH\sim \triangle ABC$, hence $\frac{AE}{AB}=\frac{EH}{BC}$. Because $AD\perp BC$, $\angle ADG=90^\circ$. Since $EH\parallel FG$, $\angle AMH=90^\circ$, so $AM\perp EH$. Again, since $EH\parallel FG$ and $AD\perp BC$, $DM=EF=EH=x$, and $\frac{AE}{AB}=\frac{AM}{AD}$, so $AM=6-x$. Using $\frac{AE}{AB}=\frac{EH}{BC}$, we get $\frac{EH}{BC}=\frac{AM}{AD}$, so $\frac{x}{12}=\frac{6-x}{6}$, hence $x=\boxed{4}$, therefore $EH=4$.
raw_record.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure, the base side BC of triangle ABC is horizontal, point A is above, and there is a right-angle mark at A; square EFGH is located inside the triangle, FG lies on BC, E is on AB, H is on AC, EH is parallel to BC, and EF and GH are vertical. Then reason: Let the side length of the square be EH=FG=EF=GH=x. It is known that BC=12, and the area of triangle ABC is 36. Taking BC as the base, the height AD satisfies (1/2)·12·AD=36, so AD=6. Because FG is on BC and the height EF of the square is x, the distance from BC to EH is x, so the height of the upper small triangle AEH relative to BC is 6-x. Also because EH is parallel to BC, triangle AEH and triangle ABC are similar, and the corresponding bases and heights are proportional: x/12=(6-x)/6. Solving gives 6x=72-12x, 18x=72, x=4.
